description: odoo-ai-agents hooks - SessionStart readiness probe + browser-MCP permission self-apply + state-root planning-permission self-apply + ETHOS @import injector + guarded legacy-state-root migration + UserPromptSubmit intent detector + SubagentStop grounding enforcement & continuation nudge & resource-teardown gate & terminal-status telemetry + PreToolUse delegate reminder & coordinator source-write deny & unowned-lease-mutation deny + Stop continuation nudge & browser-teardown advisory + PermissionDenied refused-give-back advisory + SessionEnd allocator gc crash-backstop. The SessionEnd hook only SPAWNS a detached worker and returns in milliseconds, so its `timeout` here bounds that spawn ONLY - the reaping's real bounds live in the script, because a SessionEnd hook is aborted once the batch's other hooks finish regardless of the timeout declared here (see the script's own header for the measurement). The drive-to-done and browser-teardown hooks are ADVISORY (never hard-block; parse-continuation.sh in particular has a HARD CONTRACT to never block - see its own header). There are exactly TWO PreToolUse hard denies, each matcher-scoped and each refusing one shape. (1) block-coordinator-code-write.sh, matcher-scoped to Edit|Write|MultiEdit|NotebookEdit|Bash, refuses production-source authoring by an agent the agent-role SSOT declares role=coordinator or role=spawner, Bash-mediated writes included (redirect, tee, sed -i, dd, cp/mv, git apply/patch, interpreter one-liners), because a gate that skipped Bash would look enforcing while the breach walked past it. (2) block-unowned-lease-mutation.sh, matcher-scoped to Bash, refuses a SUBAGENT's `allocator.py release` that names no owner (no --run-id / --session anywhere in that command segment) and any --force / --force-forget / reap-orphans --yes override from a subagent - the enforcement half of the allocator ownership guard, after a dispatch with a documentary brief released a live lease it had never acquired and destroyed the database. It is deliberately identity-free rather than keyed on a per-agent allow-list, because the agents that legitimately drive the allocator sit on both sides of the role line; acquire, bind, park, resume, heartbeat, gc and a list-only reap-orphans are never refused. Both headers state the residuals they provably cannot catch. Agent dispatch itself is NEVER denied at any depth: a subagent may launch its own children (that is how odoo-coding -> odoo-coder -> teammates runs), and the launcher ends its turn and is woken with the child's result. No other tool is ever denied (Bash with run_in_background: true stays free - it is how odoo-instance-ops launches builds, and that parameter is real on the Bash tool and has no equivalent on agent dispatch), and the hook fails open on any unreadable payload. Its sibling remind-delegate.sh is unchanged and stays ADVISORY-only, always emitting the no-opinion value 'defer'. There are THREE SubagentStop hard blocks, all narrow and all scoped to the subagent only (never main): (1) the instance-teardown gate, which fires only on a live, non-shared lease that the SUBAGENT ITSELF provisioned (correlated from its own acquire/bind/heartbeat --run-id) at a turn end that does not forward INSTANCE_HANDLE inside its continuation fence. This gate is STATUS-BLIND: it reads the ledger and the forwarded handle, never the status value, so DONE, NEEDS_NEXT, a stopped-run report (BLOCKED or NEEDS_CONTEXT), an out-of-enum value, and a turn with NO machine-readable status at all are ALL gated alike. BLOCKED and NEEDS_CONTEXT were an unconditional pass until a harness permission denial on the allocator give-back verb turned that door into a silent unowned leak; being unable to RELEASE is not being unable to NAME A CATCHER, and forwarding the handle is text in the dispatch's own fence - no tool, no permission, no live process - so the tightening traps nobody. Its sibling permission-denied-teardown.sh is what tells a dispatch this, at the moment its give-back verb is refused. Main-context / orchestrator-owned leases are NOT hard-gated, they are reclaimed by the SessionEnd gc backstop, which reaps a dead owner pid immediately and falls back to the allocator TTL only when liveness cannot be verified at all (a different host, or no pid recorded); (2) enforce-grounding.sh's OSM-grounding-lie gate, which fires once when a subagent's artifact CLAIMS OSM grounding but its transcript shows zero OSM tool calls (self-gating; silently approves any non-Odoo-shaped subagent - see the script's own header); and (3) enforce-background-wait.sh's unwakeable-wait gate, which refuses a SUBAGENT stop while the payload's session-wide `background_tasks` array still lists a `type: shell` entry with `status: running` whose task id the SUBAGENT'S OWN `agent_transcript_path` shows the Bash tool handing it. That gate never fires on main (the root IS woken when a background command finishes) and never on a `type: subagent` entry (an agent child does wake the launcher that stopped for it) - it exists because the Bash tool's own "you will be notified when it completes" line is written for the root and does not hold for a dispatched agent, whose SubagentStop IS the end of its dispatch; its own header states the residuals, chiefly a command backgrounded outside the Bash tool (a bare `&`, `setsid`, `nohup`), which never becomes a task id and is invisible to it. The PermissionRequest matcher's browser-family alternation (chrome-devtools|playwright|pagecast, each optionally -headed) is a JSON-literal mirror of scripts/lib/browser_prefixes.py STATIC_SERVERS / scripts/lib/browser-mcp-servers.sh BROWSER_MCP_ALL_SERVERS (JSON cannot source either file) - keep the three lists in sync when a browser family is added or removed (V-19).
